\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{волосы} (vólosy)}{волосы (vólosy)}]{\ru{волосы} (vólosy) — hair}

\label{lesson:RU-C30-hair}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for the belly, then the Russian for a tooth.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{волосы}}
\textbf{\ru{волосы}} (\emph{vólosy}) — \textquotedblleft{}hair\textquotedblright{}. Plural, like English \textquotedblleft{}locks\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{волосы}} is the plural of \emph{\ru{волос}}, \textquotedblleft{}a hair\textquotedblright{}, $\leftarrow$ Proto-Slavic \emph{*volsŭ} — inherited. Vasmer compares Avestan \emph{varəsa-}, \textquotedblleft{}hair\textquotedblright{}. Russian \emph{-\ru{оло}-} faces Church Slavonic \emph{-\ru{ла}-} again: the church form is \emph{\ru{власы}}, an old word for \textquotedblleft{}hair\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{палец} (pálets)}{палец (pálets)}]{\ru{палец} (pálets) — a finger}

\label{lesson:RU-C30-finger}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a tooth, then the Russian for hair.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{палец}}
\textbf{\ru{палец}} (\emph{pálets}) — \textquotedblleft{}a finger\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{палец}} $\leftarrow$ Proto-Slavic \emph{*palĭcĭ} — inherited; older Russian texts use it for \textquotedblleft{}thumb\textquotedblright{} (Sokolova, in Trubachev's note to Vasmer). It is usually tied to Latin \emph{pollex}, \textquotedblleft{}thumb\textquotedblright{}, though Vasmer notes doubts about that link.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{шея} (shéya)}{шея (shéya)}]{\ru{шея} (shéya) — the neck}

\label{lesson:RU-C30-neck}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for hair, then the Russian for a finger.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{шея}}
\textbf{\ru{шея}} (\emph{shéya}) — \textquotedblleft{}the neck\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{шея}} $\leftarrow$ Proto-Slavic \emph{*šija} — inherited. Vasmer thinks it probably first meant \textquotedblleft{}collar\textquotedblright{}, from the root of \emph{\ru{шить}}, \textquotedblleft{}to sew\textquotedblright{}; the links proposed with Latin and Albanian words he calls unreliable.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{cousinweb}
